messages:
alex r: noticed apiserver 5xxs and P95 climb in eu-west1 around 03:04 UTC. controller-manager queue length spiking.

sre-bot: alert: apiserver_requests_5xx_rate increased 6x in eu-west1 (03:03-03:07).

sophia: we started a bulk GPU node onboarding at 03:00 (batch=150) via infra-provisioner, default parallel attaches.

omar: pulling NAT metrics - ephemeral ports close to limit. conntrack entries high. suspect NAT exhaustion + attach storm.

omar: ```
Conntrack entries: 203456
Nat ephemeral in-use: 64600/65535
TCP TIME_WAIT skew observed
```

riley: storage team reported elevated NVMe write latency during same window; several PVs had attach ops queued.

sophia: infra-provisioner logs show attach concurrency spikes ~3-4x normal at 03:01-03:05.

alex r: plan: pause onboarding, cordon new nodes, reduce controller-manager concurrent-reconciles in eu-west1 to 6. Also add temporary iptables SNAT rule to use spare NAT IPs if available.

sophia: pausing job now (03:08 UTC). cordoned 120 nodes.

omar: after pausing, conntrack entries dropped ~45k in 6m. apiserver P95 back to ~200ms by 03:16. etcd leader flip at 03:05 aligns with the peak, likely triggered by backlog on apiserver and slow lease renewals.

riley: mitigation notes: 1) add attach rate limiter to infra-provisioner, 2) increase NAT pool / enable ephemeral port reclaim tuning on proxies, 3) schedule large onboarding outside scheduled etcd compaction windows, 4) update runbook to reduce controller concurrency during bursts.

sre-bot: incident-mitigation: onboarding paused + controller-manager concurrency reduced -> degraded->recovered at 03:16. severity: warning.

alex r: will open INF-3019 for infra changes and RUNBOOK-22 for the controlplane steps. assigning owners. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
